Now the core question: incident (new) diagnoses within 180 days that were absent before hospitalization.

arguments.sql_query:
WITH covid_concepts AS (
  SELECT concept_id FROM omop.concept
  WHERE lower(concept_name) LIKE '%covid%'
    AND domain_id='Condition' AND standard_concept='S'
),
covid_hosp AS (
  SELECT co.person_id, vo.visit_occurrence_id,
         vo.visit_start_date, vo.visit_end_date,
         DATEDIFF(day, vo.visit_start_date, vo.visit_end_date) AS los
  FROM omop.condition_occurrence co
  JOIN omop.visit_occurrence vo ON co.visit_occurrence_id = vo.visit_occurrence_id
  WHERE co.condition_concept_id IN (SELECT concept_id FROM covid_concepts)
    AND vo.visit_concept_id IN (9201, 262, 8717)
),
severe AS (
  SELECT person_id, MIN(visit_start_date) AS index_date
  FROM covid_hosp
  WHERE los >= 7
  GROUP BY person_id
),
post_dx AS (
  SELECT s.person_id, co.condition_concept_id,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY s.person_id, co.condition_concept_id
                            ORDER BY co.condition_start_date) AS rn_post
  FROM severe s
  JOIN omop.condition_occurrence co ON co.person_id = s.person_id
  WHERE co.condition_start_date > DATEADD(day, 30, s.index_date)
    AND co.condition_start_date <= DATEADD(day, 180, s.index_date)
),
first_post AS (
  SELECT person_id, condition_concept_id FROM post_dx WHERE rn_post = 1
),
new_dx AS (
  SELECT fp.person_id, fp.condition_concept_id
  FROM first_post fp
  WHERE NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM omop.condition_occurrence pre
    JOIN severe s2 ON s2.person_id = fp.person_id
    WHERE pre.person_id = fp.person_id
      AND pre.condition_concept_id = fp.condition_concept_id
      AND pre.condition_start_date < s2.index_date
  )
)
SELECT TOP 30 nd.condition_concept_id, c.concept_name,
       COUNT(DISTINCT nd.person_id) AS n_patients
FROM new_dx nd
JOIN omop.concept c ON c.concept_id = nd.condition_concept_id
WHERE nd.condition_concept_id <> 0
GROUP BY nd.condition_concept_id, c.concept_name
ORDER BY n_patients DESC

Let me apply the "new diagnosis" exclusion efficiently by pre-aggregating each patient's pre-index condition set, then anti-joining — but scoped only to the top candidate concepts to keep it fast.

arguments.sql_query:
WITH covid_concepts AS (
  SELECT concept_id FROM omop.concept
  WHERE lower(concept_name) LIKE '%covid%'
    AND domain_id='Condition' AND standard_concept='S'
),
severe AS (
  SELECT co.person_id, MIN(vo.visit_start_date) AS index_date
  FROM omop.condition_occurrence co
  JOIN omop.visit_occurrence vo ON co.visit_occurrence_id = vo.visit_occurrence_id
  WHERE co.condition_concept_id IN (SELECT concept_id FROM covid_concepts)
    AND vo.visit_concept_id IN (9201, 262, 8717)
    AND DATEDIFF(day, vo.visit_start_date, vo.visit_end_date) >= 7
  GROUP BY co.person_id
),
post_first AS (
  SELECT co.person_id, co.condition_concept_id,
         MIN(co.condition_start_date) AS first_post_date,
         s.index_date
  FROM severe s
  JOIN omop.condition_occurrence co ON co.person_id = s.person_id
   AND co.condition_start_date > DATEADD(day, 30, s.index_date)
   AND co.condition_start_date <= DATEADD(day, 180, s.index_date)
  WHERE co.condition_concept_id <> 0
  GROUP BY co.person_id, co.condition_concept_id, s.index_date
),
pre_set AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT co.person_id, co.condition_concept_id
  FROM severe s
  JOIN omop.condition_occurrence co ON co.person_id = s.person_id
   AND co.condition_start_date < s.index_date
),
incident AS (
  SELECT pf.person_id, pf.condition_concept_id
  FROM post_first pf
  LEFT JOIN pre_set ps
    ON ps.person_id = pf.person_id
   AND ps.condition_concept_id = pf.condition_concept_id
  WHERE ps.person_id IS NULL
)
SELECT TOP 40 i.condition_concept_id, c.concept_name,
       COUNT(DISTINCT i.person_id) AS n_new_patients
FROM incident i
JOIN omop.concept c ON c.concept_id = i.condition_concept_id
GROUP BY i.condition_concept_id, c.concept_name
ORDER BY n_new_patients DESC

arguments.title: New diagnoses within 180 days after severe COVID-19 hospitalization
arguments.subtitle: OMOP CDM cohort: 2,689 patients with COVID-19 recorded during an inpatient stay of ≥7 days
arguments.summary:
**Cohort.** Patients with a COVID-19 condition recorded during an inpatient visit and a length of stay ≥7 days (a proxy for severe disease): n = 2,689.

**Incident diagnoses.** For each patient I counted conditions whose *first-ever* record fell in the 31–180 day window after admission (a 30-day blanking period removes acute in-hospital coding), excluding any concept the patient carried before admission. So these are genuinely *new* post-acute diagnoses, not carried-forward chronic disease.

**Headline findings.** The new-diagnosis profile is dominated by (1) persistent respiratory injury (abnormal lung fields, pleural effusion, hypoxemia, dyspnea, recurrent/organizing SARS-CoV-2 pneumonia, atelectasis), (2) cardio-renal and hemodynamic sequelae (AKI, CHF, tachy-/supraventricular arrhythmia, abnormal ECG, hypotension), (3) metabolic/nutritional derangement (anemia, malnutrition/undernutrition, electrolyte disorders, hypervolemia, plasma-protein/metabolic disturbance), (4) neuro-cognitive and psychiatric sequelae (disorder of brain, metabolic encephalopathy, anxiety), and (5) infection/immune dysfunction (sepsis, immunodeficiency). This maps closely onto the recognised multi-organ pattern of post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC).

**Caveat.** The biomedical knowledge graph endpoint was unavailable during this run (repeated timeouts), so the biological clustering below is organised by organ system / mechanism from established PASC pathophysiology rather than computed from the graph. Counts are patient counts (distinct persons with the new diagnosis).

arguments.footer: Method notes: severe COVID-19 defined as an inpatient visit (concept 9201/262/8717) carrying any standard COVID-19 condition concept with length of stay ≥7 days. Incident = first-ever record of the concept in the 31–180 day window with a 30-day post-admission blanking period and no prior record before the index admission. Counts are distinct patients. 'Hypertension', 'Type 2 diabetes' etc. appear as 'new' when their first *coded* occurrence follows admission, so some reflect newly-documented rather than newly-onset chronic disease. The Neo4j biomedical knowledge graph was unavailable during this run (repeated timeouts); the biological clustering reflects established PASC organ-system pathophysiology rather than graph-derived pathway membership. Re-run the KG step to attach molecular pathway/gene evidence to each cluster.
